4. // FrameAddress — Specifications
5. //
6. // A `FrameAddress` is an opaque, page-aligned physical frame address: a `Copy`
7. // value object that names one physical frame. Its abstract value is exactly the
8. // frame's base physical address as an unbounded integer (`FrameAddress@ : int`,
9. // defined by the `View` impl below, delegating to the inner
10. // `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>`). Callers exchange it through two equivalent
11. // identities of that single integer:
12. //
13. //   * the raw physical address — `into_raw_value` / `from_raw_value`; and
14. //   * the frame index — `into_frame_number` / `from_frame_number`, where the
15. //     index is `address / PAGE_SIZE` (`spec_frame_number`).
16. //
17. // The frame-index helpers (`spec_frame_number`, `spec_from_number`), the frame
18. // representability bound (`spec_max_frame_number`), the `arch` `FrameNumber`
19. // projection (`spec_frame_raw_value`) and the universal address projection
20. // (`spec_addr`) are all reused from the sibling `phys` / `aligned::page`
21. // specifications, so every member of the address tower speaks the same
22. // vocabulary.
23. 
24. verus! {
25. 
26. use crate::hal::mem::{
27.     spec_addr,
28.     spec_frame_number,
29.     spec_from_number,
30.     spec_frame_raw_value,
31.     spec_max_frame_number,
32. };
33. 
34. // ── Canonical page/frame size ────────────────────────────────────────────────
35. //
36. // `spec_page_size()` is the canonical frame size, re-exported from
37. // `crate::hal::mem` and shared by the whole address tower
38. // (`FRAME_SIZE == PAGE_SIZE == spec_page_size()`). It is an external-bottom
39. // trust boundary: a per-architecture runtime constant with no concrete value at
40. // the spec level. Kept here (verification material) so the exec source carries
41. // no cfg-gated verification constructs, mirroring `phys.rs`.
42. pub uninterp spec fn spec_page_size() -> int;
43. 
44. // `::arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE` is the runtime page size, tied to `spec_page_size()`.
45. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE ] -> (result: usize)
46.     ensures
47.         result == spec_page_size(),
48. ;
49. 
50. // ── View ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51. //
52. // `FrameAddress` abstracts to a single mathematical integer: the frame's base
53. // physical address, delegated from the inner `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>`.
54. // `closed` so the two-level newtype delegation does not leak; callers obtain a
55. // usable `int` (`fa@`) for arithmetic, frame indexing, set membership, and
56. // comparison.
57. impl View for FrameAddress {
58.     type V = int;
59. 
60.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
61.         self.0@
62.     }
63. }
64. 
65. // ── Well-formedness invariant ────────────────────────────────────────────────
66. //
67. // Two structural guarantees every constructor establishes and callers rely on:
68. //
69. //   * page alignment (`self@ % spec_page_size() == 0`) — relied on at every MMU
70. //     / page-table / allocator site, never re-checked; and
71. //   * frame-number representability
72. //     (`spec_frame_number(self@) <= spec_max_frame_number()`) — the load-bearing
73. //     fact that makes `into_frame_number` total (its inner
74. //     `FrameNumber::from_raw_value(..).unwrap()` never panics) and lets the frame
75. //     allocator use the result directly as a bitmap / refcount index.
76. //
77. // Stated purely over the abstract address `self@`, independent of the inner
78. // representation.
79. impl FrameAddress {
80.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
81.         &&& self@ % spec_page_size() == 0
82.         &&& spec_frame_number(self@) <= spec_max_frame_number()
83.     }
84. }
85. 
86. // ── `hal::mem` library-edge trust boundary ───────────────────────────────────
87. //
88. // `<PhysicalAddress as Address>::from_raw_value` is a method of the external
89. // `sys::mm::Address` trait, below this module's verification boundary; a
90. // trait-impl method cannot be body-verified in place without marking the whole
91. // `impl Address for PhysicalAddress` verified (pulling its unsupported
92. // `usize as *const u8` sibling casts into scope — see
93. // `verus-ai-logs/verus-unsupported.md`). It is therefore specced here with
94. // `assume_specification`, mirroring the trust boundary the codebase already
95. // draws for `<PageAligned<T> as Address>::into_raw_value` (`page.spec.rs`) and
96. // `::arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE` (above).
97. //
98. // On success it validates and wraps without rounding: the abstract address
99. // equals the raw value (`r@ == value`) and the validated address has a
100. // representable frame number (`spec_frame_number(r@) <= spec_max_frame_number()`,
101. // i.e. it lies within physical memory). On failure (`value` is not a valid
102. // physical address) no address is produced; the dynamic validity predicate is
103. // platform-specific, so the failure condition is left unconstrained —
104. // `from_raw_value`'s sole caller only branches on `Ok`/`Err`. Stated through
105. // `PhysicalAddress`'s `View` (`r@`) rather than the universal `spec_addr` to
106. // avoid a definitional cycle (`spec_addr<PhysicalAddress>` would depend back on
107. // the very `impl Address for PhysicalAddress` this method belongs to);
108. // `FrameAddress::from_raw_value` bridges `r@` to `spec_addr` in its body.
109. // Removed when `hal::mem` is verified.
110. pub assume_specification[ <PhysicalAddress as Address>::from_raw_value ](
111.     value: usize,
112. ) -> (result: Result<PhysicalAddress, ::sys::error::Error>)
113.     ensures
114.         match result {
115.             Ok(r) => r@ == value as int
116.                 && spec_frame_number(r@) <= spec_max_frame_number(),
117.             Err(_) => true,
118.         },
119. ;
120. 
121. // `<PageAligned<T> as Deref>::deref` is the auto-deref that resolves
122. // `self.0.into_frame_number()` to `PhysicalAddress::into_frame_number`. It is a
123. // trait-impl method of the external `core::ops::Deref` trait, below this
124. // module's verification boundary, specced here as a trust boundary. It is pure
125. // projection: the borrowed inner address has the same abstract value as the
126. // wrapper (`spec_addr(result) == addr@`). Stated through the universal
127. // `spec_addr` projection rather than `result@`, because a bare `T: Address`
128. // carries no `View<V = int>` bound (mirrors `page.spec.rs`).
129. pub assume_specification<T: Address> [
130.     <PageAligned<T> as ::core::ops::Deref>::deref
131. ](addr: &PageAligned<T>) -> (result: &<PageAligned<T> as ::core::ops::Deref>::Target)
132.     ensures
133.         spec_addr(result) == addr@,
134. ;
135. 
136. } // verus!
